(a) Maintenance of Primary, Backup, and Attrition Reserve Inventory of Aircraft.—Subsection (a) of section 131 of the John Warner National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2007 (Public Law 109–364; 120 Stat. 2111) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1)—
            (A) in subparagraph (A), by striking “and” at the end; 
            (B) in subparagraph (B), by striking the period at the end and inserting a semicolon; and 
            (C) by adding at the end the following:“(C) shall maintain in a common capability configuration a primary aircraft inventory of not less than 63 such aircraft, a backup aircraft inventory of not less than 11 such aircraft, and an attrition reserve aircraft inventory of not less than 2 such aircraft; and“(D) shall not keep any such aircraft referred to in subparagraph (C) in a status considered excess to the requirements of the possessing command and awaiting disposition instructions.”; and  
        (2) by adding at the end the following:“(3) Definitions.—For purposes of paragraph (1):“(A) The term ‘primary aircraft inventory’ means aircraft assigned to meet the primary aircraft authorization to—“(i) a unit for the performance of its wartime mission;“(ii) a training unit primarily for technical and specialized training for crew personnel or leading to aircrew qualification;“(iii) a test unit for testing of the aircraft or its components for purposes of research, development, test and evaluation, operational test and evaluation, or to support testing programs; or“(iv) meet requirements for special missions not elsewhere classified.“(B) The term ‘backup aircraft inventory’ means aircraft above the primary aircraft inventory to permit scheduled and unscheduled depot level maintenance, modifications, inspections, and repairs, and certain other mitigating circumstances without reduction of aircraft available for the assigned mission.“(C) The term ‘attrition reserve aircraft inventory’ means aircraft required to replace anticipated losses of primary aircraft inventory due to peacetime accidents or wartime attrition.“(4) Treatment of retired aircraft.—Of the aircraft retired in accordance with paragraph (1)(A), the Secretary of the Air Force may use not more than 2 such aircraft for maintenance ground training.”.  
    (b) Notice of Retirement.—Subsection (b)(1) of such section is amended by striking “45 days” and inserting “60 days”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the "Notice of Retirement" provision creates a participatory process, but it only changes a waiting period for a notice that, in this defense authorization context, most likely goes to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The rest of the section sets aircraft inventory minimums and definitions for the Secretary of the Air Force. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.

opus.w: The section sets Air Force aircraft inventory minimums, defines inventory terms and limits how retired aircraft may be used. None of this involves anyone outside the federal government. The 'Notice of Retirement' change only lengthens a notice period, and the notice goes to Congress, which is inside the government. There is no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body or consultation with outside parties.
opus.s: (b) Notice of Retirement.—Subsection (b)(1) of such section is amended by striking “45 days” and inserting “60 days”.
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** One could misread subsection (b), "Notice of Retirement," as a procedural step that involves others before a decision is made. It doesn't hold up. The underlying provision (section 131(b) of the FY2007 NDAA) requires notice to the congressional defense committees, which are inside the federal government. In any case, this amendment only changes the notice period from 45 to 60 days. Everything else sets aircraft inventory levels and definitions. No state, company, expert or member of the public takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section primarily defines inventory levels for military aircraft and adjusts an internal notice period for retirement. It does not require consultation with or participation from entities outside the federal government. The 'Notice of Retirement' is an administrative procedural change within the Department of the Air Force, not a public participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Notice of Retirement.—Subsection (b)(1) of such section is amended by striking “45 days” and inserting “60 days”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Notice of Retirement" implies a public notification or consultation process. However, the text only specifies the duration of the notice period (changing it from 45 to 60 days) and does not specify who receives the notice or that it involves outside parties. It is likely an internal administrative notice. Furthermore, the rest of the section deals with inventory levels and definitions, which are internal management decisions. There is no requirement for public comment, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states/tribes.
